cases.about: Her obituary said, "Heather was a joyful and loving mother, daughter, sister, aunt, and friend. Her deep joy and love of nature manifested itself in her becoming a certified arborist, with her plan to have a career in urban forestry. She enjoyed the outdoors and spent much of her free time with her daughter and friends at Florida lakes, springs and beaches."

cases.name: Kira Anne Radcliffe
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Kira's special love was her mother. In Kira's free time, her love of life constantly expressed itself in her singing, her drawing, and her happy personality. Her happiest times were playing at local beaches, lakes, and springs with her mother and their friends. She was in the first grade at Glen Springs Elementary school, and enjoyed gymnastics at the YMCA. She was a vision in motion with bouncy blond curls and a perpetual smile. She was a bright, happy little girl who liked to sing and make up songs about the things in her life. She loved to draw pictures of rainbows, and also loved dolphins, and butterflies. But the love of her life was her Mommy. Their favorite activity was going to the beach, and watching the Gators."

cases.name: Brittany Avery-Hoisington
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Brittany loved music, her family, her friends and above all, helping people. Brittany lit up every room and lifted up people in every circumstance. “Bitters”, as she was affectionately known, was a kind, loving, caring, and giving person. If someone needed a couch, she offered it. If someone needed a snack or food, her pantry was stocked and open. If someone needed a friend, she was there. She could be counted on, unless it was to actually be on time. Brittany brought people together and always made them laugh. Her quick wit was unequalled and infectious. Brittany was a free spirit. The loss of Brittany’s amazing soul touches her family and friends and will do so indefinitely. Her memory will live on through those memories she created with while she was with us. The only way we could avoid these feelings of devastating loss, would be to not have known her.
Brittany was a joy; she was stimulating; she was challenging and worth it. Her intellect was shocking and humble. Her sense of humor and sense of joy will turn hundreds of “moments” into a lifetime of precious memories and heartwarming laughter."
